stories.headline: Nvidia tells server partners to pause shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as US tightens export controls
EvolveMAS: A Unified Self-Evolution Framework for Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems

sentences.text: You have two stories today: Nvidia pausing server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries and a framework for self-evolving decentralized multi-agent systems.
First, the biggest story this morning.
Nvidia has told its server partners to pause shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.
Reporting from the Wall Street Journal, relayed by TechCrunch, says Dell and Super Micro were among the manufacturing partners told to hold server shipments.
Chinese companies have been using Nvidia chips remotely from data centers in those countries, a loophole the U.S. Commerce Department closed earlier this month.
The Institute for Progress estimates those remote data centers supply about 24 percent of China's AI computing power.
If you're tracking export controls, this is the one to watch.
Next, something for your work on agent memory.
EvolveMAS is a framework that lets decentralized groups of language model agents adapt and reuse what they've learned.
The paper argues that existing approaches often build adaptation for one particular kind of interaction at a time.
Agents there have to adjust to other agents at test time and reuse past experience, whether cooperating, mixing motives, or opposing each other.
Since you follow agent memory, the reuse of accumulated experience is the part to pay attention to.
Now to chips and China's AI labs.
Next, a nuclear story, since you're tracking SMR licensing.
And finally, one from outside your usual beat.
Which of these would you like to dig into?
